sections.heading: C - Your Vehicle
sections.markdown:
## C - Your Vehicle

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
An owned vehicle requires Florida registration, a license plate, and a Florida title unless held by an out-of-state lienholder; non-residents who start work or enroll children in Florida public school have ten days to register with Florida insurance and title proof, and out-of-state vehicles need vehicle identification number verification except new vehicles, new or used mobile homes, trailer-type recreational vehicles, and trailers or semitrailers under two thousand pounds [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
Service centers title and plate by weight and type, plates stay current with papers aboard, dealers file for buyers while private buyers file themselves, titles precede plates, and out-of-state licensees license first [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Renewals run yearly or biennial to the birthday midnight, mobile homes and semis to December 31, fleets to June 30, open 90 days early, and recheck insurance [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A02
Required gear spans dual brakes, low beams 150 ahead and 1,000 seen, high beams 450 and 1,000, tails 1,000, brake lamps 300 by day, plate lamps 50, signals 500, horns 200, mirrors 200, wipers, plain safety glass, tint caps 25 and 35, and 3/32 tread [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A02
Prohibited vehicle equipment includes red lights visible from ahead, blue lights, more than two spotlights, fender, cowl, fog, or other extra lights, sirens, bells, or whistles, mufflers emitting smoke or audible beyond fifty feet, and signs, posters, or stickers on windshields or windows unless required by law [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A03
Driver-visible television and worn headsets are also banned, manuals answer car-specific questions, and airbags assist rather than replace belts [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A03
Warning-only helpers flag blind spots, closing gaps, lane drift, and reverse cross traffic without ever acting [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A03
Acting helpers brake for frontal and pedestrian crashes and nudge back drifting lane changers [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A04
Reverse braking guards backing, adaptive cruise spaces the gap, centering holds the middle, and keeping corrects straying wheels [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A04
Crash callers summon rescuers, auto beams swap with traffic, and backup cameras never replace mirrors and head turns [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A04
Anti-lock drivers stomp, hold, and steer while electronics pump faster, and pumping or lifting kills the assist [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A05
Plain-brake drivers pump sliding stops, bumper heights step 22 through 30 inches by car and truck weight, and emission tampering is illegal [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A05
Light trailers need twin reflectors plus a brake lamp when hidden, while heavy ones add clearance and marker lamps with rear reflectors [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A06
Towed brakes answer the driver and self-stop on breakaway, heavy pole trailers lamp and reflector both sides, and stop lamps run two except pre-1972 singles [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A06
Drawbars must hold the load, span at most 15 feet except for long objects, and flag chains and cables with a 12-inch white square [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A06
Loads must never drop, shift, leak, or escape, loose hauls wear covers, and log trucks chain down [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A06
Rear overhangs past four feet flag 18-inch red squares by day and lamp 500-foot reds with 100-to-600-foot reflectors by night and rain, with log poles adding an always-on amber strobe [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A06
Car loads never pass the left fender line and pass the right by at most 6 inches [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0050]

items.why: Section five is equipment and towing recall served by standard flashcards and quizzes; no separate practice mode is needed.

corpus_stability.reason: The Official Florida Driver License Handbook is a dated revision (rev. 08/2023) reissued at most annually, so vehicle equipment rules change at most once per year.
